A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MobileIPL work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable matching across layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original MobileIPL evaluations on AITZ, AMEX and AndroidControl, together with ablations, reasoning analyses and training-cost results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds an accuracy-and-rollout comparison involving MobileIPL, SPO-Chain and GRPO.

M1.justification: The CoaT stages, instruction evolution, reward propagation, preference-pair filtering and iterative DPO procedure are retained. v4 expands the loss/update description in Section 3.3; the PDFs do not establish a changed procedure, and Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain AITZ, AMEX and AndroidControl, including the same unseen-app and unseen-task evaluations and screenshot-based instruction-evolution data. The added efficiency comparison identifies no additional dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: v4 newly evaluates SPO-Chain in Table 6 alongside MobileIPL and GRPO. GRPO previously appeared in the AndroidControl comparisons. Existing comparator memberships are retained; newly discussed TCPO, TreePO and TreeRL are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds rollouts per sentence as an efficiency measure in the new three-method comparison and reports SPO-Chain's best temperature as 1.4. Original benchmark settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix D are unchanged. Detailed controls for the added comparison are not specified.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an efficiency-versus-accuracy analysis and qualitative observations about SPO-Chain's sensitivity to temperature and cut-point probabilities. Existing component, low-resource, reward and sampling analyses, plus Appendix H case studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change. Existing standard-deviation analyses and Figure 3 displays are retained; new Table 6 provides point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports accuracy/rollouts of 69.15/~27 for MobileIPL, 68.03/~54 for SPO-Chain and 66.29/8 for GRPO. MobileIPL's 69.15 already appears in v3 Table 1. Existing benchmark, ablation, appendix and figure results are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 explicitly defines the conditional T-DPO likelihood-ratio loss in Equation 15; v3 specified the preference pairs and invoked DPO without this equation. This is a limited formal specification addition. Existing reward derivations and other mathematical definitions are retained, with no new proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about thinking-level preference learning, instruction evolution, three-benchmark performance and out-of-domain generalization. The additional comparison supports the work without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v4 newly argues that MobileIPL offers a favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-off and explains that SPO-Chain's higher-temperature exploration produces longer outputs and slower sampling. Existing interpretations of PRESS recovery, annotation instability and equivalent valid actions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly documents the policy/reference T-DPO loss and mentions SFT loss during policy updates. Section 4.4 supplies SPO-Chain's temperature of 1.4. Existing implementation settings, prompts, training-time information and dataset-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations and positioning against TCPO, TreePO, TreeRL and SPO, emphasizing thought–action consistency and sampling efficiency. Additional agent-related references expand Section 2.1, while the overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 adds focused T-DPO and efficiency explanations, revises part of the related-work discussion and makes small terminology, typo, contact and conference-header edits. Most prose and the overall section and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 6, renumbers subsequent tables, enlarges Figure 1 and changes the placement and sizing of several tables and figures. Ablation and parameter-search tables become separate wider displays. The seven figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves methodological clarity through the explicit T-DPO loss and adds a direct SPO-Chain efficiency comparison absent from v3, while preserving existing results and appendix evidence. Limited protocol detail and uncertainty reporting constrain the new efficiency claims, so the overall benefit is useful but limited.
